{{nihongo|'''Inu Shrine'''|伊奴神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

It is identified with the “Inu Shrine” listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} under {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}{{ill|Yamada district, Owari|Q11470699|qid=Q11470699|lt=Yamada District}}.

Because of its name “Inu” (dog), stone dog statues stand in front of the main hall, and the shrine is popular with people born in the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Year of the Dog}} as well as dog lovers. In particular, on {{ill|New Year's Day|af|Nuwejaarsdag|ar|رأس السنة الميلادية|ary|راس لعام لميلادي|arz|راس السنه الميلاديه|az|Yeni il günü|bcl|Aldaw kan Bagong Taon|bh|न्यू इयर|bn|নববর্ষ (গ্রেগরীয় বর্ষপঞ্জি)|bo|གནམ་ལོ་གསར་ཚེས།|cbk_zam|Dia de Nuevo Año|ceb|Adlaw sa Bag-ong Tuig|ckb|ڕۆژی ساڵی نوێ|cy|Dydd Calan|da|Nytårsdag|el|Ημέρα της Πρωτοχρονιάς|eo|Novjara Tago|es|Día de Año Nuevo|et|Näärid|eu|Urte berri egun|fa|روز سال نو|fi|Uudenvuodenpäivä|gv|Laa yn Vlein Noa|he|ראש השנה האזרחית|hi|नव वर्ष का दिन|hy|Նոր տարվա օր|id|Tahun Baru Masehi|is|Nýár|ja|元日|kaa|Jańa jıl kúni|kcg|A̱tuk Mam A̱lyia̱ A̱fai|ko|새해 첫날|ks|نیہِ ؤریُک دۄہ|lb|Neijoerschdag|lo|ວັນຂຶ້ນປີໃໝ່|mai|नव वर्ष कें दिन|ml|പുതുവർഷ ദിനം|ms|Hari Tahun Baharu|my|နှစ်ဆန်းတစ်ရက်နေ့|nn|Nyttårsdag|no|Første nyttårsdag|pdc|Neiyaahrsdaag|ru|День Нового года|rue|Новый Рӯк|sco|Ne'er's Day|simple|New Year's Day|smn|Uđđâvuođpeivi|sr|Нова година (1. јануар)|sv|Nyårsdagen|ta|புத்தாண்டு நாள்|te|నూతన సంవత్సర రోజు|th|วันขึ้นปีใหม่|tl|Araw ng Bagong Taon|tr|Yılbaşı|uz|Yangi yil kuni|vi|Tết Dương lịch|wuu|元旦|zh|元旦|zh_classical|元旦|zh_yue|元旦|qid=Q196627}} in the Year of the Dog, large numbers of worshippers visit the shrine<ref>{{Cite news|title=“‘Dog’ shrine extremely busy: twice as many shrine maidens, ten times the amulets prepared”|url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASKDC00BJKDBOIPE00G.html|publisher=The Asahi Shimbun Company|date=2017-12-21|language=Japanese|accessdate=2018-01-01}}</ref>.

{{Quotation|Reverently enshrining the secret Inō Myōjin: Ukanomitama no Kami<sub>Wakumusubi no Kami, Uke Mochi no Kami</sub>, respectfully revised.|Genroku 8 ridge tag}}
{{Quotation|Reverently enshrining the secret Kumano Myōjin: Ihe-nami no Kami<sub>Hayatama no O no Kami, Amakumahito no Kami, Koto-saka no O no Kami</sub>, respectfully revised.|Genroku 8 ridge tag}}

The early Edo-period document *{{ill|Kanbunmuramuraoboegaki|Q137766629|qid=Q137766629}}* states, “Inō Village… Kumano Gongen, shrine precincts designated as tribute land”{{Sfn|名古屋郷土文化会|1984|pp=1-2}}. It is said that the Yamada family served as shrine priests until the {{ill|Bakumatsu|Q804558|qid=Q804558}}{{Sfn|名古屋郷土文化会|1984|pp=1-2}}.

In the mid-Edo period, {{ill|Amano Sadakage|ja|天野信景|qid=Q6535030}} identified the shrine with “Inu Shrine” of Yamada District in the *Engishiki Jinmyōchō*, and this view thereafter became the accepted theory. Because the location was Inō Village and the name resembled “Inu,” it appears that the shrine was identified as such. The *{{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|Q11041830|qid=Q11041830}}* records “Junior Third Rank Upper, Inu Tenjin”{{sfn|「角川日本地名大辞典」編纂委員会|1989|p=177}}{{sfn|有限会社平凡社地方資料センター|1993|p=127}}. {{ill|Tsuda Masanari|Q22123474|qid=Q22123474}} and others have advanced the theory that the original Inu Shrine was actually the {{ill|Tenjin|Q1305727|qid=Q1305727}} enshrined in the auxiliary sanctuary of this shrine. The *{{ill|Owarishi|Q137855962|qid=Q137855962}}* suggests that Kumano Gongen was merely a {{ill|Massha|Q135009906|qid=Q135009906}} until the {{ill|late Heian–Kamakura period|Q11395861|qid=Q11395861}}, but after it fell into ruin and was enshrined within the main sanctuary, it came to be treated as the principal deity. It also points out that place names and shrines with the same names as this shrine, such as “Inō-gō” and “Inu Shrine,” existed in {{ill|Izumo Province|ar|إزومو (مقاطعة)|ca|Província d'Izumo|cs|Provincie Izumo|de|Provinz Izumo|es|Provincia de Izumo|fa|ولایت ایزومو|fr|Province d'Izumo|gl|Provincia de Izumo|id|Provinsi Izumo|it|Izumo (provincia)|ja|出雲国|ka|იზუმოს პროვინცია|ko|이즈모국|lt|Idzumo žemė|nl|Izumo (provincie)|no|Izumo|pt|Província de Izumo|ru|Идзумо (провинция)|simple|Izumo Province|sk|Izumo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Изумо|tr|Izumo (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ідзумо|wuu|出云国|zh|出雲國|zh_classical|出雲國|zh_min_nan|Izumo-kok|zh_yue|出雲國|qid=Q582846}} {{ill|Aika district|Q11595889|qid=Q11595889}}, as recorded in the *{{ill|Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|Q11395858|qid=Q11395858}}*, suggesting a possible connection with this shrine.

=== Rituals ===
* {{ill|Sagichō Fire Festival|ja|左義長|pl|Sagichō|qid=Q9332740|lt=Sagichō}}: Second Sunday of January
* Tamanushi Inari Grand Festival: First Sunday of March <ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.inu-jinjya.or.jp/event/tamanushi.html|title=玉主稲荷大祭|publisher=伊奴神社|language=日本語|accessdate=2018-01-01}}</ref>
* Chinowa Ritual: Saturday and Sunday in late July <ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.inu-jinjya.or.jp/event/shinzi.html|title=茅輪神事|publisher=伊奴神社|language=日本語|accessdate=2018-01-01}}</ref>
* Annual Grand Festival: Second Sunday of October <ref name="例祭"/>
* Doll Memorial Service: First Sunday of December <ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.inu-jinjya.or.jp/event/ningyou.html|title=人形供養祭|publisher=伊奴神社|language=日本語|accessdate=2018-01-01}}</ref>

=== Other ===
The shrine grounds were designated a “Nagoya City Green Space Conservation Area” on {{ill|1980|Q2439|qid=Q2439|lt=November 25, 1980}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa}} 55) <ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.nagoya.jp/ryokuseidoboku/cmsfiles/contents/0000016/16086/tokuryoku.siteijyoukyou.H29.3.pdf|page=1|format=PDF|title=特別緑地保全地区の指定状況 （平成29年3月1日現在）|author=名古屋市役所緑政土木局 緑地部 緑地維持課 緑化指導審査係|publisher=名古屋市|accessdate=2018-01-01|language=日本語}}</ref>, and is surrounded by many trees, including an 800-year-old {{ill|Castanopsis|Q1065400|qid=Q1065400|lt=Japanese chinquapin}}.

During the {{ill|Ōzumō|Q10937013|qid=Q10937013|lt=Grand Sumo}} {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=名古屋場所}}, {{ill|Isegahama stable (2007)|Q11378930|qid=Q11378930|lt=Isegahama stable}} uses the shrine as lodging, and sumo wrestlers can be seen practicing on the {{ill|Dohyō|Q832429|qid=Q832429|lt=dohyō}} within the precincts.

The shrine is known for prayers for safe childbirth, fertility, marital harmony, and household safety. After a safe childbirth prayer, worshippers offer prayers in front of the dog statues within the precincts.

=== Access ===
* {{ill|Nagoya Municipal Subway|Q1144874|qid=Q1144874|lt=Nagoya Municipal Subway}} {{ill|Tsurumai Line|Q1043806|qid=Q1043806|lt=Tsurumai Line}}: Get off at {{ill|Shōnai-dōri Station|Q863241|qid=Q863241|lt=Shōnai-dōri Station}} <ref name="アクセス"/>.
* {{ill|Nagoya Municipal Bus|Q11414982|qid=Q11414982|lt=Nagoya City Bus}}: Get off at “Eko” bus stop on routes Meieki 13, Sakae 11, or Sakae 13, or at “Inō-chō” bus stop on route Sakae 13 <ref name="アクセス"/>.
